title: CPU-GPU queue harmonizer: compact prefetch aggregation and threadpool deconflict
creator: Rohit Menon
description: This ticket implements a host-side 'queue harmonizer' that consolidates small prefill/copy requests into aligned pinned-slab transfers, reduces threadpool contention by introducing an affinity-aware executor, and surfaces kernel selection hints to the runtime to avoid spurious kernel probes during prefill. The goal is to reduce host-induced latency variance in prefill->decode path and lower CPU overhead per request.
technical_notes: Design: 1) Introduce a compact prefetch aggregator in host bridge: group adjacent token prefill memcpy ops into single staged pinned-buffer transfer. 2) Replace multiple competing threadpool work-queues with an affinity-aware executor: lane-per-request with token-priority queueing and cooperative stealing disabled for prefill lanes. 3) Add lightweight kernel-hint metadata on request path to skip kernel prober on common seq-len/model-variant combos. 4) Use single-producer multi-consumer ring for DMA fence signaling to reduce syscall fanout. Implementation in two phases: POC with toggles, rollout via runtime-1.24 feature flag. Memory model: pinned slab pool with eviction by LRU and size-bucketed pages to avoid fragmentation. Trade-offs: increases pinned memory footprint (~10% of host RAM for heavy workloads) but reduces p99 latency significantly; complexity added to host bridge code path.
acceptance_criteria: prefill p99 latency reduced by >=25% on text-generation 1k token load test
CPU sys% decreased by >=20% under 500 concurrent small-chat requests
end-to-end throughput >= baseline or within 5% degradation
feature toggled via runtime-1.24 and can be disabled per-customer
